pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented in full — three to four kettlebell workouts a week built around his existing adjustable bell, plus a five to fifteen minute daily mobility routine targeting 'your shoulders, your tennis elbow and also just your overall body alignment.' The prospect engaged on mechanics rather than value: 'I have one kettlebell. Do I have to buy another one to have two kettlebells?' and 'I asked you because I saw a squat exercise when it uses two kettlebells.' On the check-in he confirmed fit but had to re-confirm what was being asked: 'Yes. You're talking about to improve my mobility, right?'

Rep pitched a whole-foods protocol with small tweaks to his existing eating window, explicitly acknowledging he was already doing well. Prospect agreed without questions or pushback: 'Yes, because of the diet, it's very important.' No tie back to his own goal, so short of enthusiastic.

The full one-to-one stack was delivered — 30-minute intake with Trevor, app-tracked workouts, filmed form reviews with 24-hour feedback, Thursday live community workouts, and 'Trevor is going to be banging on the door like hey what are you doing Mike where you're not doing the workout.' Prospect confirmed he was following and, asked directly whether any questions came up, said 'No.' He did volunteer a positive on the teach-a-man-to-fish framing — 'Well, I saw in the email I received that you told, well, he told us how to do a program, right?' — but did not tie the accountability structure to his own situation.

anchors.raw: Yeah, because I am saving for buying a car for my daughter, my older daughter, that's why. I would have to take from that.
anchors.note: Proposed label: competing_committed_capital. Not a competitor product but the number actually in the prospect's head when he heard $6,000 — a car fund for his eldest daughter earmarked for purchase by year end, plus college books and fees due 'this and the next month'. It is the anchor that decided the call, and the rep chose to attack it directly rather than work around it.

anchors.raw: I have been learning, as I told you, on magazines or books or videos, but this is the first time I approach.
anchors.competitor: YouTube / fitness magazines / a self-study over-40 summit ('alpha plus or something like that')
anchors.note: Proposed label: free_self_directed_substitute. His entire training education to date has cost nothing, and he had four years of gym results from it. He rated the expert as worth more than videos ('it's not the same to watch many videos on YouTube') but had no reference point for what coaching costs — 'I didn't have an idea of the cost of the program' — so $6,000 landed against a zero-dollar baseline.

anchors.raw: I am converting it to my currency.
anchors.note: The prospect converted $6,000 into roughly 100,000 Mexican pesos live on the call and the rep then re-priced in that figure ('is it worth the 100,000 Mexico currency for you'). Restating the price in the larger local number made the anchor heavier, not lighter. Worth noting at scale for non-US prospects.

unmet_demand.want: Confirmation that kettlebell training can fully substitute for his current barbell and dumbbell bodybuilding split rather than sit alongside it
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised the substitution assumption directly — 'Well, I understand that kettlebell can substitute that' — and asked whether he should keep the bodybuilding workouts. The rep asked the question, never answered it, and later described the programme as three to four kettlebell workouts a week without addressing what happens to the gym split he has run for four years and enjoys.

unmet_demand.want: An age-specific protocol built for a 47-year-old's joints and recovery rather than a generic programme
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This was his stated reason for wanting a coach — 'It's very different if I was 25 years old, but at my age, I have to train according to my age, my joints, my schedule.' The programme almost certainly does this via the one-to-one intake, but nobody said so explicitly; the age-specificity of the protocol was never named as a feature.

unmet_demand.want: To pay for a six-month transformation without disturbing money already committed to his family
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The only structures offered were three payments of $2,000 or six of $1,200 with interest — both of which draw on the committed capital. There is no lower-cost or longer-dated entry point in the offer for a fit, motivated prospect whose constraint is liquidity rather than intent.
